newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Steel Mills sees strong Q4 shipments.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Steel Mills sees strong Q4 shipments.

text.p: Oregon Steel Mills Inc said Monday it expected strong rail and pipe shipments in its fourth quarter partly to offset higher manufacturing costs caused by a power outage.

At the end of September, Oregon Steel's CF&I Steel unit lost the use of one of two main transformers that supply electricity to its melt shop. Full electrical power is expected to be restored by early December.
"The transformer outage at CF&I has been a setback to improving our cost structure there," said Thomas Boklund, chief executive officer of Oregon Steel.

"However, we are anticipating strong rail shipments as well as continuing strong seamless pipe shipments during the fourth quarter of 1996, which we believe will somewhat mitigate the increase in manufacturing costs due to the outage," he added.

Earlier Monday, Oregon Steel reported third-quarter profit rose to $6.4 million, or $0.24 a share, from $2.0 million, or $0.10, in the year-earlier period. Revenues slipped to $187.7 million from $188.5 million.
